resources.string: Limb vein cutaway
Representative calf vein · Longitudinal cutaway, toward the heart at top
Calf vein segment
This segment represents a vein running through the calf. Veins carry blood back toward the heart.
Paired valve leaflets
In this example of a valved limb vein, blood moving toward the heart pushes the two leaflets aside. If flow reverses, the leaflets come together to limit backflow. Not all veins have valves.
Venous lumen
Blood flows through this inner channel. Veins generally have wider lumens and thinner walls than their accompanying arteries.
Vein wall
An inner lining faces the blood. Outside it lie a relatively thin layer of smooth muscle and a supporting layer of connective tissue.
Skeletal muscle capillary bed
Systemic capillaries · Between skeletal muscle fibers, with one enlarged
Feeding arteriole
This small arterial branch supplies the capillary bed between muscle fibers.
Capillary branch
These narrow channels exchange oxygen, nutrients, and wastes with the surrounding muscle tissue. Unlike pulmonary capillaries, they do not border an alveolar air space.
Collecting venule
Multiple small channels merge into this venule, which drains the muscle capillary bed toward larger veins.
Continuous endothelium
A single layer of flattened endothelial cells forms the lining of this muscle capillary. Its channel is narrow enough for red blood cells to pass in single file.
Air–blood barrier layers
Respiratory membrane · Enlarged thin region between alveolar air and blood
Type I alveolar epithelium
Flat type I cells line most of the alveolar surface. Their thin extensions form the air-facing tissue layer of the barrier.
Fused basement membranes
In this thin region, the basement membranes of the alveolar epithelium and capillary endothelium join, leaving very little tissue between the cells.
Capillary endothelium
Flat endothelial cells line the blood side. Oxygen diffuses from alveolar air through the barrier into blood, while carbon dioxide moves in the opposite direction.
Alveolar capillary mesh
Pulmonary capillaries · Section through alveoli with a septal surface exposed
Pulmonary arteriole
This small pulmonary arterial branch delivers oxygen-poor blood to the capillary network in the alveolar walls.
Septal capillary mesh
Short, interconnected capillaries lie inside the thin walls shared by neighboring alveoli, not in the air spaces. The exposed mesh shows how much of the septum is available for gas exchange.
Pulmonary venule
The capillary network drains into small venules. These collect oxygen-rich blood and carry it toward the pulmonary veins and left atrium.
